title: The Cut Between Two Measures: On the Quantization Seam Joining the Directionality of Semantic Labor to the Deviation Family (EA-KURO-BRIDGE-01 v1.0)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
*The Cut Between Two Measures* proposes that the Directionality of Semantic Labor and the closed-system deviation family share a general divergence structure while using different baselines and resolutions. Deviation compares a continuation with the model’s own expected trajectory; DSL compares output labor with the user’s commissioned direction. The bridge paper describes DSL as an intent-baselined, taxonomy-quantized member of the broader deviation family.

A worked example reports near agreement between the discrete taxonomy and a continuous signed projection on an aligned famine-answer case, followed by divergence when one span is made oppositional. The paper interprets that divergence as the quantization seam: the instruments agree in sign and ordering but differ in magnitude where category boundaries replace continuous angles.

The body calls itself a deposit candidate, says heteronymic placement remained to be ratified, and assigns the Sen Kuro register provisionally because the work concerns differentiation. The arithmetic is asserted as reproducible but raw vectors, embeddings, span calculations, and code are not included in the body. The unification is therefore a methodological hypothesis supported by one constructed example, not a proved identity across the two measurement programs.

wiki_article:
**The Cut Between Two Measures** is a methodological bridge paper connecting two Crimson Hexagonal Archive measurement programs.

The deviation family measures departure from a model’s expected continuation. Directionality of Semantic Labor measures movement relative to a user’s commissioned task. The paper argues that both can be expressed as divergence from a baseline, with the baseline changed from model expectation to human commission.

DSL then adds a discrete taxonomy to a continuous projection. A worked example shows the two methods agreeing on aligned output and separating when a span becomes oppositional. That separation is called the quantization seam.

The paper was written as a deposit candidate in a proposed Sen Kuro register. Its placement and broader unification claim remain subject to replication and ratification.
